question: Can I do tayammum when I'm embarrassed to do wudu, and how is tayammum performed?
asked: Is it allowed to do tayammum when we are embarrassed about doing wudu, or when it is awkward to do wudu? And if so, how is tayammum done? For example, a sister wearing hijab who is in a place where she cannot do wudu.
answer:
Realize that tayammum is a divine gift that Allah gave to our ummah. He did not give it to any other ummah before us. It is a gift that demonstrates Allah wants to make things easy for us and not to make things difficult. And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala legislated tayammum in the fourth or fifth year of the hijrah, on the return of the expedition of the Prophet ﷺ where Aisha was there and her necklace broke. The famous expedition where her necklace broke and she went out to search for it, and then what happened, happened. This is the expedition where the tayammum verses were revealed.

So when her necklace broke and she announced to the Prophet ﷺ she doesn't have a necklace, the Prophet ﷺ camped and he sent people to go find the necklace. Right? This is the love that he had for Aisha. Even though it was not an expensive necklace, it had sentimental value. Turns out the necklace was underneath the camel. They couldn't find it until the camel stood up; when the camel stood up, they found it. So it had fallen down and the camel sat on it.

Because they were delayed, they ran out of water, because they were one stop away from Medina and they were supposed to get to Medina within two, three, four hours, so they had enough water to last them there. Because of the delay, they ran out of water, and they didn't have water to do wudu. So the sahaba went to Abu Bakr and began chastising him: "Look at what your daughter has done. Because of your daughter, we're all delayed."

And this is the reality of frustrated people. They take their anger out, firstly when they shouldn't, and secondly on the wrong people. And believe me, I know this all the time. They always take their anger out on the wrong person. What has Abu Bakr as-Siddiq got to do with it? It was the Prophet ﷺ that said we're going to remain here. But who's going to criticize him? So they go to Abu Bakr and say, "Look at what your daughter has done. Because of her necklace we are stuck here."

And when the delay continued and they ran out of water, Allah reveals Surah Ma'idah, verse 6, and in it Allah says:

> وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرْضَىٰ أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ

And when this verse came down, the same sahaba who criticized Abu Bakr went back and apologized, and they said, "This isn't the first blessing that has come because of your family, O Abu Bakr. All of us have benefited, that we don't have to use water in extreme circumstances anymore."

So Allah revealed tayammum in this time frame, and it is in the Qur'an. And the meaning of tayammum, the linguistic meaning, is to intend something, to want to do something. And the reason why we call tayammum tayammum is that all we need to do is intend to do wudu, and we do the very minimal things, and we have wudu. Simply wishing to do wudu, and then with tayammum we have wudu. You just have to wish you're in tahara, and you just do something symbolic, as we'll say, and you're in tahara. That's why tayammum is called tayammum.

The verse is comprehensive. It mentions the causes, it mentions the cases, and it mentions the procedure. All of it is in the verse. Allah mentions two things in the verse: if you are sick, or you're traveling and you don't have water. This verse mentions these two cases. Some scholars have added a third, which is a part of this, which we're going to come to.

And the verse also mentions whether you have used the restroom or you have touched women. This is in the Qur'an, which means tayammum takes the place of both wudu and ghusl. This is in the Qur'an. This is the beauty: the verse is so small, and yet so much is coming from it. When to do tayammum, how to do tayammum, and the causes of tayammum: all three are mentioned in this verse.

So Allah is saying, even if you come from the bathroom, or, in the language of the Qur'an, you have touched women (Allah does not use vulgarities; touching women means you have been intimate), so in your state of janabah, and you don't have water, then what should you do? Then intend to lift your janabah, or state of not being in tahara, with sa'idan tayyiban, pure sa'id. Wipe your face and your hands with it. So this shows us tayammum.

Now, Sahih Bukhari mentions that once 'Ammar ibn Yasir was on a journey and he had to do ghusl. He woke up in a state of janabah, he had a night dream, and he didn't have enough water. So 'Ammar said, "I removed my garments in a faraway location, nobody was there, and I then turned naked in the sand, all over the sand, my body, to do tayammum, and I then prayed. Then I went back to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what I had done." And the Prophet ﷺ said, "All you needed to do was this." And then he showed him: the Prophet ﷺ put his hands on the sand, blew, and then he wiped his face and his hands, because that's all you needed to do. The hadith is in Bukhari and Muslim.

This shows us tayammum is symbolic. Dust doesn't become water. You don't roll over; you don't take sand and go like this. No, tayammum is symbolic. That's why it is called tayammum: you intend, and so it happens.

And tayammum is a gift to this ummah that no ummah had before. Our Prophet ﷺ said: this earth has been made my masjid, and this earth has been made a source of becoming clean. So the hadith goes: whatever person of my ummah has to pray, he will have his place to pray, and he will have the instruments to clean him with him.

Now, to us, we take it for granted. The previous nations, and to this day the Orthodox Jews follow this: you cannot just pray anywhere, you need a congregation. You cannot just use any water; you need to use water that is found with a long list of conditions. Their janabah, their ghusl, they need to do it in their synagogues. They cannot do it the way that we do; they cannot do it at home. When the ladies have to do ghusl after the monthly cycle, they have to go to the synagogue to do ghusl, because it's a special type of water that is not just tap water.

So the Prophet ﷺ is saying, for us, our Lord has gifted us. What has He gifted us with? Wherever we are, we can pray. We can pray anywhere. When it's time for salah, we pull the car over and we just pray, and it is allowed as long as the earth is pure. And wherever we are, we can purify ourselves. If we have water, alhamdulillah. If not, tayammum. This is a gift and a blessing to make life easy for us. It was not given to any nation before us.

So how does one do tayammum? It goes without saying, obviously, as usual, all of the madhhabs have minor differences. We can just ignore them. I just want to teach you the basics for now, and whoever is an advanced student can go study within the madhhab.

When is tayammum done? Scholars say three circumstances. In reality it is two, as the Qur'an says; the third one is under number two. The first one, explicit in the Qur'an: you are traveling and you don't have water. Why did Allah say you are traveling and you don't have water? Because it is impossible to live at a location for a time frame without water. Water, you need it; within two, three days you will die. It is impossible to have life without water. However, it is very common that you are traveling and you have to ration water. So the meaning of not having water is that you have to save water to drink rather than to just waste it. This is the meaning here: that you don't have water enough for you to purify yourself.

And this is something the collective group will decide: "Look, we're this many people, we have this much water, and from now till we get to the next stop, we don't have enough for wudu." This is something collective, common sense. And if you err on the side of caution, no big deal, because you need water to live. So this is something you make the decision on if you're alone, or the group makes the decision.

So for example, you have Dhuhr and Asr, three and a half hours, and there's a stop. In America, basically everywhere you go you'll find water, generally speaking, unless you're in the Mojave Desert or something and there's four hours; then in that case you may do tayammum. But generally speaking, if you can have access to water, you cannot do tayammum, if you're going to find water on the way, if it is something reasonable for you to obtain.

Now, a question: if you're going from point A to point B, and your house is in that direction, and water is only at point C, and that's 200 miles the other way, you are not obliged to go opposite to your house. If you don't have water, you may do tayammum. You have just the water in your car to drink, and for whatever reason you forgot to have water to do tahara, or you thought you'd get to a gas station, and you're driving and there is no gas station. Are you required to drive an amount or a quantity that is unreasonable?

What is unreasonable? You use your common sense. What is unreasonable varies from person to person. If you're with kids in the car, maybe 45 minutes out of your way is unreasonable. If you're all alone and you have the rest of the day, like, "Okay, inshallah, I'll just go," you make a decision. It's not a big deal. This is something where, inshallah, you make your personal, conscious decision. But you are not required to travel an unreasonable way out of your journey. If it's on your journey, then obviously you're going to get there. Out of your journey, you're not required to do that. So if you don't have water, or you don't have enough water to use: number one.

Number two, Allah says if you're sick. There are a few sicknesses where you cannot use water, for example severe burns. You cannot just pour water on a severe burn. For example, the hadith is in Abu Dawood: a man was in a battle and his skull cracked open. They bandaged his wound, and then he had to do ghusl. He woke up in the state of janabah; he had to do ghusl. So he said, "Do I have to put water? It's supposed to be dry. Do I have to put water?" One of the people around him said, "Well, you're in the state of janabah and you have to do ghusl. I don't find any excuse for you."

And by the way, this is the problem of literalism and of jahalah. This is the problem when you don't study fiqh and the shari'ah and you take level one: if it says it, it must be the case. Fiqh is not copy and paste. Fiqh is extracting the laws from the text.

So one of the sahaba said, "Yeah, you have to do the janabah ghusl. That's it, you do it." So he poured water on his head. It's a festered wound. What happened? The wound festered, became putrid, and he died before they got back to Medina. They buried him. When the Prophet ﷺ found out, he became angry, and he said, "They murdered him." By that fatwa, they murdered him. "They killed him," I should say. "May Allah curse them": it's a statement. It's legitimate anger: your foolishness and overzealousness harmed a Muslim.

Then he said, "Why didn't they ask if they didn't know? Why didn't they ask if they didn't know?" They just gave a fatwa: "I think it must be the case." And then the famous hadith, the same hadith: "The cure to ignorance is asking questions." Allah says in the Qur'an, ask the people of knowledge. Don't just become a mini Google mufti, fatwa Wikipedia. Don't do that. Ask the people who have studied fiqh, and they will give you the response.

So the second reason: if there is a wound or a state where you cannot put water on it, you may do tayammum on top of it.

And then some 'ulama have added a third, which is under number two. And they have said, if the weather is so cold, and the water in those days would be freezing, if you have to crack open the ice and the wind is blowing and you have to do wudu, you might actually cause extreme hardship to yourself. In such circumstances, they said, you may do tayammum. Now these days, if you're at home, you can turn the hot water on, and you don't have the desert wind, freezing wind, blowing at you.

I have had to do this, by the way, and it's a judgment call, again, between Mecca and Medina in February and whatnot. Sometimes it is freezing cold in the desert and it's not easy to do wudu. If you have the himmah and you think it's going to be okay, you may quickly do it. And if you think, especially for a child or a lady that's sensitive or pregnant, you feel it's not safe for them, in that circumstance, again, it's a judgment call, if you think it's not safe. And in reality this comes under number two, because you're causing harm to yourself, and you're not going to cause harm to yourself.

So these are the conditions where you may do tayammum. **Being embarrassed is not one of the reasons for tayammum.** So if you feel awkward to do wudu in a restroom where there are other ladies there or whatnot, that is not an excuse not to do wudu. You must do wudu. Of course, you can always take a cup of water and go somewhere else and do wudu as well. And all of you should learn how to do wudu from a cup of water. All you need, frankly, is even less than half a cup. Maybe one day I'll show you. You can easily do wudu with a small quantity of water, and you can do it behind your car, whatever, no problem.

So that is when you do tayammum. Tayammum is also done as late as possible before the salah. So you delay the tayammum until you have to pray. And this is common sense: you don't do tayammum and then two, three hours later you pray, because what if you were to find water? What if you come across a gas station? You want to pray, and you're like, "Okay, there's three hours, I'll just do tayammum now." You don't know what's going to happen in those three hours before you pray. So the scholars say you delay your tayammum until right before your time to pray, and then you do tayammum.

And then there's a bit of a controversy: does your tayammum last to the next salah if you don't find water? There's a controversy, and you have both opinions, and it's just safer. It takes less than two seconds to do tayammum, so you might as well just do it before the next salah.

So tayammum is symbolic, and the Prophet ﷺ showed 'Ammar ibn Yasir how to do it. What did the Prophet ﷺ do? He hit his hands on the ground once, with the intention to do tayammum. You just hit your hands. And then he wiped (in the hadith it says) his face, and then his hands up until the wrists. So up until the wrists, not until the elbows. So it's just symbolic. And there are other versions that say he wiped his hands and then his face. So again, both positions are found as to which one goes first.

But the point being, the goal is not to transfer the sand to your face. That's not the goal. The sand does not become water. It's symbolic. In the hadith of 'Ammar, he blew. Why would you blow? To remove even whatever is there. It is an issue of symbolism.

And what is tayammum done with? The Malikis and the Hanafis said that tayammum can be done with any material that is on the surface of the earth, because Allah says, "Fa-tayammamu sa'idan tayyiban," and sa'id is everything that's on the surface of the earth. It doesn't have to be actual sand. They said a rock, a stone, even the edge of a cliff or a mountain: you can just tap it, and that is your tayammum. Anything that is connected to the earth and is there.

My own teacher Ibn 'Uthaymin would always remark: anything that dust settles on. Anything that dust settles on; it's symbolic. Now the issue comes: does dust settle on cloth? That's a good question. I'm not going to answer it. But suppose it was not the cloth on here, suppose it was just this table here, and it's in the open and public; it means dust is settling on it. Our teacher Ibn 'Uthaymin allowed this; he would say that. But if you want to be safe, and you want to get something, soil, any type of, even rocks or something, that's fine. Some madhhabs are more strict about what you do; no problem.

So you put your hand over there, and then if you want to get rid of it, even blow it off so that there's nothing coming, no problem. It is symbolic. And then you just wipe your face and your hands. One or two madhhabs say you should also do this; some said it's sunnah and some said it's good. But the hadith of 'Ammar is clear. The hadith of 'Ammar, which is in Bukhari and Muslim: the Prophet wiped and wiped, and that's it. And this is, inshallah, sufficient.

So once again, tayammum is allowed when you don't have access to enough water, or when you are too sick or it's dangerous to use water. And all that needs to be done is intention, tapping once (once again, some of them have said once for the hands and once for the face, but these are trivial issues), tapping once, and then you can wipe your hands and wipe your face, and that is done, and then you just pray.

And think about the psychology of tayammum. If Allah had willed, He could have said, "Just pray as you are." But we would have felt something in our hearts: we don't have wudu, we don't have tahara. So to put our conscience at ease, Allah revealed a symbolic tayammum that takes one second, well, one and a half, that's it, just to make our hearts comfortable that you have tried to do tahara.

And that's why it is called tayammum: to intend, to try something. What's the verse in the Qur'an? "Wa la tayammamul-khabitha minhu tunfiqun": don't intend the khabith. Tayammum here means intend. That's what I wanted to say. The shahid is that tayammum is used in the Qur'an to mean intention. So Allah revealed to us an ease, to ease our conscience.
